chunks: And Hell is made visible to those who had gone astray.

key_terms.الْجَحِيمُ: Hell, specifically referring to a deep or fiery part of Hellfire
key_terms.لِلْغَاوِينَ: To those who are astray or misguided, referring to disbelievers or sinners who deviated from the right path

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Hell is 'made visible' to the misguided on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Ash-Shu'ara is often linked with the concept of 'Tajalli al-Haqq' (the manifestation of Truth), where Hell is not merely a place but a revealed reality to those who rejected divine guidance. The term 'al-ghawin' (the misguided) specifically denotes those who deviated due to arrogance or ignorance, highlighting the psychological and spiritual state that leads to this ultimate visibility of their fate. This scene serves as a powerful deterrent, reinforcing the justice of God in making the consequences of one's choices undeniably clear.
